newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 4.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Hungarian Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti met with Czech Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny and Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec in Prague yesterday. Keleti confirmed Hungary's interest in Czech L-159 fighter aircraft and in further military cooperation with the Czech Republic.

- The golden cup in the Pivex '97 trade fair in the category of 12 percent light lager went to Hostan from Znojemsky Pivovar, and Gambrinus from Plzensky Prazdroj was chosen as the best 10 percent beer.
- Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny began an investigation yesterday to find allegedly lost documents which were given to the Czech Republic by NATO.

PRAVO - Education Minister Ivan Pilip met with representatives of the school workers union on Monday and did not succeed in reaching an agreement. After the meeting, the head of the union, Jaroslav Rossler, confirmed that the union will decide on another approach on March 7 to achieve a raise in wages.

- In the past three days, the crown has weakened sharply. From the maximum of 5.51 percent above parity, which the crown reached in the middle of February, the crown slipped to below two percent above parity.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - According to the Finance Ministry, the cost of a litre of petrol will probably increase by one crown in 1998 over this year, a package of cigarettes also by one crown and strong alcohol by three crowns. Beer prices should also increase. This is due to a proposal for increasing consumer taxes on fuel, alcohol and tobacco products, which will give the state more than seven billion crowns.

- Reliable information leaked from the Defence Ministry about the military order for a staff information system, which could cast doubt upon the whole tender and lead to its cancellation, is being investigated by the secret service, and they do not rule out that they will pass it on to the police.

LIDOVE NOVINY - After a meeting yesterday with Agriculture Minister Josef Lux, the Agrarian Chamber withdrew its intention to begin civic disobedience today if its requests for half of consumer taxes on petrol to be returned to agriculture were not fulfilled.

- The general director of the Czech Trade Association, Bretislav Ostadal called on the vice-chairman of the cabinet Josef Lux to support the current management of Czech Railways. Ostadal's letter to Lux was in reaction to Lux's request that Rudolf Mladek resign from his position as general director.
